newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's MCI index slips over - 100 b.p. as TWI eases.
newsitem.headline: NZ's MCI index slips over - 100 b.p. as TWI eases.

text.p: The New Zealand Monetary Conditions Index (MCI), measuring the degree of variance in money and foreign exchange market conditions from the Reserve Bank's assumed levels for monetary policy, fell to more than 100 basis points equivalent below the RBNZ's preferred mix on Monday.

At about 11.57 a.m. (2357 GMT) the index, as measured by a Reuters formula correlated to the Reserve Bank's, slipped to -1.02 as the New Zealand dollar's Trade Weighted Index (TWI) dropped below 67.30 versus about 67.48 at the opening.
The MCI had indicated about -90 b.p. in early trade.

A number of economists across the New Zealand market have been predicting during the last few trading sessions that the Reserve Bank would be inclined to seek to curb the market-led easing of conditions from current levels if the MCI remained in the region of 100 b.p. away from the desired line for any length of time.
In early May a series of falls in the 90-day bill rate below 7.00 percent sent the MCI dipping to near -1.00 and spurred the RBNZ to comment on May 12 that conditions had become too easy.
A reweighting of market conditions then occurred with the TWI softening slightly and bill rates rising.
According to RBNZ's last comment on monetary conditions in March, its desired mix of conditions is a 7.50 percent 90-day bank bill rate and 68.0 on the TWI.
By 12.20 p.m. (0020 GMT) today the mix was at 7.03 percent on the 90-day bill rate and 67.35 on the TWI, giving an MCI value of -0.95.
